chunks: And what we see of Your creation, and wonder at it because of Your might, and describe it as (a result of) Your great authority, and what is hidden from us of it, of which our sight has fallen short, which our intelligence has not attained, and between which and ourselves curtains of the unknown have been cast, is far greater.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between visible creation and hidden divine realities in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) articulates the epistemological limits of human perception, distinguishing between the tangible creation and the transcendent divine essence that remains veiled from the intellect. This reflects the Shia theological emphasis on the incomprehensibility of God's true nature (Dhat), where sensory and rational faculties reach their boundary before encountering the infinite. The text serves as a reminder that the 'greatest' reality is not what is observed, but what is concealed by the veils of ghayb, urging believers to look beyond the apparent to the ultimate source of Sultan (authority).
